darwin.span_check: OK. 75% reach = 54 km. Farthest spot is darwin-18 Fogg Dam at 50.9 km; others: darwin-5 Territory Wildlife Park 31.6 km, darwin-14 Berry Springs 31.3 km, darwin-19 Big Boxing Crocodile 30.6 km. All inside. Fogg Dam is the tight one (3 km margin).

tagline_fact.fact: Darwin is Australia's northernmost capital, the only tropical capital city, on Darwin Harbour and the Timor Sea.

description_facts.fact: Capital and largest city of the Northern Territory; 139,902 people at the 2021 census, nearly 63% of the territory's population.
Smallest, wettest and most northerly Australian capital; serves as the Top End's regional centre. Mean annual rainfall 1,811.7 mm; mean max 32.2 C.
Overlooks Darwin Harbour, 'a harbour 5 times the size of Sydney Harbour', known for multicultural food scene, markets, outdoor sunsets.
People from more than 50 nations live there; the Australian National Trust recognised its multiculturalism as a 'multicultural icon of national significance'.
Gateway to Kakadu, Litchfield and Nitmiluk (Katherine Gorge) national parks.

Distinctive: the only Australian capital to come under substantial wartime attack; Japanese air raids began 19 Feb 1942 (64 raids in all, last 12 Nov 1943). Cyclone Tracy on 25 Dec 1974 killed 71 people and destroyed over 70% of buildings; the city has been rebuilt four times.
Traditional owners are the Larrakia people (Larrakia name Garramilla).
About 3,000 km north of Adelaide along the Stuart Highway; airport 13 km north-east of the city centre with flights to all mainland capitals plus Bali, Singapore and Dili.

whyVisit_candidates.reason: Meet saltwater crocodiles at Crocosaurus Cove

facts.fact: Crocodiles in the middle of the city (Mitchell St).
Tourism NT: 'more crocodiles in the Northern Territory than anywhere else in the world'; visit a park or take a boat to meet them.
Cage-of-death tank dive: placement bio only, not yet confirmed on operator page (research step).

whyVisit_candidates.reason: Watch the sunset at Mindil Beach

facts.fact: Beachfront sunsets at Mindil Beach Markets; Darwin sunsets are 'legendary'.
Mindil Beach Sunset Markets are the largest in the NT; run May to October, Thursday and Sunday; bring a blanket and watch the sunset on the sand.

whyVisit_candidates.reason: Swim in the clear pools at Berry Springs

facts.fact: Popular picturesque swimming spot; use goggles to spot native fish in the clear pools; monsoon-forest walk from the picnic area; about 50 km south of Darwin, 45 minutes by car; can be closed for swimming in the wet season.

whyVisit_candidates.reason: Explore Darwin's wartime tunnels and bunkers
whyVisit_candidates.spot_id: darwin-12 (Oil Storage Tunnels) or darwin-9 (Military Museum)

facts.fact: Oil Storage Tunnels: long tunnels bored into the cliff to store oil in WWII, now with historic photos; $7 (Wikivoyage, updated 2015, verify).
Wharf was bombed at 9:58 AM on 19 Feb 1942.

whyVisit_candidates.reason: See a B-52 bomber at the Aviation Museum (alternate)

facts.fact: B-52 on permanent loan from USAF, one of only two on public display outside the US; 8 km from the city.

whyVisit_candidates.reason: Spot birds on the Fogg Dam wetlands (alternate)

facts.fact: 'One of the best birding sites in the country'; Darwin region has over 400 bird species.

darwin.whyVisit_recommendation: Rank 3 so 3 reasons: (1) darwin-2 crocodiles, (2) darwin-4 sunset (a Tourism NT 'Why visit Darwin' item), (3) darwin-14 Berry Springs swim or darwin-12 wartime tunnels. Verify each has a photo; the Mindil Beach reason depends on a beach/sunset photo, not a market photo.

goodToKnow_candidates.title: Be Crocwise
goodToKnow_candidates.detail: Any Top End water may hold crocodiles; swim only where signed safe. Box jellyfish are a danger from October to May.

goodToKnow_candidates.title: Wet and dry seasons
goodToKnow_candidates.detail: The Dry runs May to October; the Wet, November to April, brings storms, humidity and cyclone risk. Book tours ahead in peak season.

goodToKnow_candidates.title: Buy a Parks pass
goodToKnow_candidates.detail: Darwin needs no permit, but day trips to Litchfield need an NT Parks Visitor Pass ($10 adult per day); NT residents are exempt.

goodToKnow_candidates.title: Drink plenty of water
goodToKnow_candidates.detail: Drink at least two litres of water a day, more outdoors; avoid walking in the hottest part of the day and wear a hat and sunscreen.

goodToKnow_candidates.title: Markets run May to October
goodToKnow_candidates.detail: Mindil Beach Sunset Markets trade Thursday and Sunday in the Dry only and jam traffic and parking; go early or take a bus.
goodToKnow_candidates.caveat: 'take a bus' is not sourced; writer should drop it or keep only 'arrive early' (also an inference). Wikivoyage page dated Jul 2015 for this listing; confirm days on operator page.

darwin.bestMonths_note: Wikivoyage: 'climatically perfect to visit from May to October'; Tourism NT: dry season May-Oct is best; most famous events (Mindil markets, Darwin Festival in August) fall then.
darwin.bestTimeBlurb_reason: The Dry, {months}, is warm and sunny with cooler nights, and the Mindil Beach markets and Darwin Festival run then; Wikivoyage notes it is nearly always about 31 C and sunny by day.

seasonalTags.pattern: Dry-season peak: Darwin and the Top End are bustling May to October with a packed events and festivals calendar; the Wet (Nov-Apr) is low season with smaller crowds and cheaper flights, accommodation and tours.
Darwin Festival is held each August (18 nights).

litchfield.span_check: OK. 75% reach = 37.5 km. Farthest spot is litchfield-6 Batchelor at 24.8 km; all other spots are well inside (waterfalls and Lost City within about 15 km).

tagline_fact.fact: Tourism NT calls it 'the waterfall capital of Australia': tumbling waterfalls, huge termite mounds and swimming holes about an hour south of Darwin.

description_facts.fact: Covers about 1,500 km2 (1,458.47 km2 per CAPAD); declared a national park (Wikipedia gives 1986 in text, infobox 29 July 1991; do not state a date); about 329,600 visitors in 2017.
Waterfalls fall from the Tabletop Range sandstone plateau; permanent spring-fed falls (Florence, Tolmer, Wangi), Buley Rockhole cascades, magnetic termite mounds and the Lost City sandstone pillars.
About 60 minutes' drive south of Darwin by Tourism NT; Wikipedia says about 100 km south-west of Darwin near Batchelor (Wikivoyage's '69 km' disagrees; do not use).
Magnetic termite mounds stand up to 2 m high, up to 100 years old, with thin edges pointing north-south to regulate temperature.
Traditional owners are the Wagait Aboriginal people; named for Territory pioneer Frederick Henry Litchfield (explored the area in 1864).
Wikivoyage: crocodiles are not as much of a threat in Litchfield as other Top End parks, but Wikipedia notes salties in the Finniss River area.
Only real way to explore is by own vehicle or hire car, or a tour from Darwin; north end by 2WD on bitumen, south end needs 4WD.

facts.fact: Best-known, one of the most popular attractions; twin falls into a large plunge pool in monsoon rainforest; 3 km loop up and over the falls; kiosk, barbecues and campground (book online).
Swimming not permitted during the wet season, 'typically from October to March', due to currents and possible saltwater crocodiles; the falls are then spectacular to watch.
Double waterfall into a plunge pool in monsoon forest; 160 steps down, or the 1 km Shady Creek Walk; flows year-round, most spectacular in the wet season and early dry.
Hundreds of mounds up to 2 m high on a flood plain; boardwalk with accessible viewing and info shelter; open daily 24 hours; also larger cathedral termite mounds nearby.

whyVisit_candidates.reason: Soak in the cascades at Buley Rockhole

facts.fact: Series of cascading plunge pools; Wikivoyage: 80 m from the car park; a popular swimming spot.

whyVisit_candidates.reason: View Tolmer Falls from the gorge rim (alternate)

facts.fact: 400 m walk to two viewing platforms; 1.6 km loop walk (about 45 min); swimming not permitted; colonies of rare ghost bats and orange horseshoe bats in the gorge.

litchfield.whyVisit_recommendation: Rank 3 so 3 reasons: (1) litchfield-1 Wangi swim, (2) litchfield-2 Florence Falls, (3) litchfield-4 termite mounds (a distinct subject for the photo; Buley Rockhole litchfield-3 is the swim alternate). Note Wangi swimming is closed in the wet season, so reason 1 should not imply year-round.

goodToKnow_candidates.title: Parks pass required
goodToKnow_candidates.detail: Visitors need an NT Parks Visitor Pass before arriving: $10 adult per day, $20 for 3 days, $5 child; NT residents are exempt.

goodToKnow_candidates.title: Wet-season swimming limits
goodToKnow_candidates.detail: Wangi Falls swimming is not permitted in the wet season, typically October to March; some areas can close from flooding. Check before you go.

goodToKnow_candidates.title: Drive in your own vehicle
goodToKnow_candidates.detail: Public transport does not reach the park. Sealed roads reach the waterfalls; the south end and Lost City need a 4WD and are dry season only.
goodToKnow_candidates.caveat: 'Public transport does not reach the park' is not stated by a source (Tourism NT says driving or a tour). Writer should use: 'Drive yourself or join a tour from Darwin.' Also 'dry season only' is for 4WD campsites/tracks closed in the wet per Wikivoyage 'Dec-Mar'; say 'tracks close when flooded'.

goodToKnow_candidates.title: Be Crocwise
goodToKnow_candidates.detail: Swim only where signed safe; saltwater crocodiles can be in unsigned waters. Tolmer Falls pool is closed to swimmers.

goodToKnow_candidates.title: Book camping online
goodToKnow_candidates.detail: All campsites at Wangi and Florence Falls must be booked online before arrival. The Tabletop Track also needs a booking and permit.

litchfield.bestMonths_note: Tourism NT: cooler weather in the Dry, May to October; some locals say April shoulder month is ultimate for camping without crowds. Park is open all year; waterfalls are most spectacular in the Wet but some areas close from flooding. Alternate range if the writer wants the swim window: May-Oct (swimming is closed Oct-Mar at Wangi so Oct is borderline; consider 5-9).
litchfield.bestTimeBlurb_reason: The Dry, {months}, has warm sunny days and cooler nights, and the pools are open for swimming; in the Wet the falls thunder but swimming at Wangi is closed and some areas flood.

seasonalTags.pattern: Dry season (May-Oct) is peak; Wet (Nov-Apr) is low season with smaller crowds (Tourism NT, whole NT).

Driving time: Tourism NT says 60 min / about 1 hour; the brief's 1.5 hours is not sourced (Wikipedia 100 km, Tolmer page '85 km as the crow flies'); Wangi is farther than the park gate.
